sentences.text: Record of the trial Court has been received.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A. no. 14729/2022, which is an application filed un section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C on behalf of the appellant Naushad for grant of  bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

The appellant has been convicted under sections 366 and 376(2)
 of IPC and sentenced to undergo seven years R.I with fine of Rs. 500/- and  ten years R.I with fine of Rs. 2000/- respectively with default stipulation

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that during trial,
 was remained on bail and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
He  is in jail since 31/10/2022 i.e. from the date of judgment.

The prosecutrix  herself admitted in her cross-examination that her name was included in  voter list ( Ex.- D/3 and D/4), which was proved by Yogesh Khilare, who  was posted as Assistant Grade-II at Election Office, Indore and the  prosecutrix also admits that she is using her voting rights since 2014.
She  did not raise any alarm while travelling with the appellant in different  places.
She remained in the company of the appellant for the period of five  days.
There is strong case in favour of the appellant.
Final disposal of th  appeal will take sufficient long time.

Under these circumstances, he prays Signature Not Verified Signed by: AMOL N MAHANAG Signing time: 1/20/2023 10:56:00 AM  2  that the application be allowed and the remaining jail sentence of the  appellant be suspended till final disposal of the appeal.

Learned GA for the respondent/State opposed the prayer for gra Naushad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166399991/
1 bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant by submitting that as per the scholar register, the prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident; FSL report is found positive and seaman and sperm were found over the salwar and viginal slides of the prosecutrix, therefore, the appellant does not deserve for bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties as also taking note of the fact that the appellant was remained on bail during and he has not misused the liberty granted to him; the prosecutrix herself admits that she is using her voting rights since 2014 and her name was incorporated in the electoral list (Ex.- D/3 and D/4) and final dispoal of the appeal is likely to take time, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant Accordingly, IA No.14729/2022 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal and it is ordered that the appellant be released on bail upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 09/05/2023 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
